summary: Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon as chief justice and first member (c. 1811–1819) and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (c. 1823–1849).

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he was a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University (c. 1974–1979) and Leiden University (c. 1979–1987), where he later held a post in 1999.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (c. 2011–2018), supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Moscow University (c. 1946–1951) and under George Roerich, he held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Oriental Studies (c. 1956–1973), and SOAS (attested 1995).

Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was active in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at East India Company College (c. 1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where he studied under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972) and served as Professor at Paris Nanterre University from around 1974 to 1993.

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol (c. 1996–1999) and earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) under Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and worked under supervisor Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017) along with several other teachers.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and completed a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg, later holding posts at Leipzig University and UC Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. Educated at Dorpat, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Harvard, he held posts at Peking University (c. 1922–1928) and directed the Sino-Indian Institute (c. 1928–1937).
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under teachers Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Yves Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist. He studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy from around 1815 to 1832 and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from around 1835 to 1854.

Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at Balliol College and with Lakshman Joo, he held fellowships and posts across Oxford, including Professor and fellow at All Souls College (c. 1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oakwood Friends School, Haverford College, and the University of Chicago (c. 1964–1973), and served as Professor of Religion/Religious Studies at George Washington University (c. 1968–2017).
Alfons Fürst (born 1961) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen from around 1982 to 1988 and held a post at the University of Münster around 2006.

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) worked in Indology and Tibetology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (c. 1936–1941) under Carlo Formichi and Giuseppe Tucci, and later conducted post-graduate research there.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) studied at Pennsylvania, Andover Newton, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD c. 1955–1963). In Buddhist and religious studies, he held posts at Harvard, Dean at IBS (c. 1986–1994), and Emeritus Professor at Hawaii.

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College, Lahore (c. 1903–1936), Honorary Librarian at Panjab University, and Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab.
